guardianfootball.description: The nature of this Scotland defeat felt far more significant than the fact it arrived at all. Sébastien Pocognoli is already in tricky territory, just four games into his tenure as Scotland head coach. Slovenia comprehensively outplayed the fragile hosts at Hampden Park, which leaves Pocognoli staring at a third-placed finish in a soft Nations League section. Brave new dawn or beginning of an error? Scotland were defensively disorganised. Their attacking play was timid. Long before full time, the 39-year-old Belgian had the look of a coach throwing darts blindly at a board. And missing. Wastefulness from Slovenia prevented Scottish embarrassment. quietus.title: Glenn Richards & The Venus Lakes – The Great Behind
quietus.description: Glenn Richards & The Venus Lakes The Great Behind The Augie March auteur debuts an energising new ensemble Despite gracing the country with a quick visit this month, Glenn Richards isn’t widely known in England. But in his native Australia, Richards is an influential songwriter with a beloved band in Augie March. Their 2006 breakthrough Moo, You Bloody Choir won the Australian Music Prize and yielded the grand, enduring singalong ‘One Crowded Hour’. Two decades on from that high-water mark, Augie March are still crafting great records, albeit self-released to considerably less fanfare. Along the way, Richards found an unlikely champion in Johnny Depp, who discovered Augie March in 2008 and…

quietus.title: Rum Music for October Reviewed by Kate Molleson
quietus.description: With our regular columnist Jennifer Lucy Allan on sabbatical, we're leaving Rum Music in the capable hands of broadcaster and journalist Kate Molleson. Here she presents her favourite new discoveries, from deconstructed tropicália to a crystalline performance of a 400-year-old masterpiece via sung quotes, gamelan and more Jessie Marino with Inga Margrete Aas & Pinquins, photo by Oliver Matlok A rare treat to guest in these pages – thanks for having me! Normally I’m lost in the minutiae of composer biographies (presenting BBC Radio 3’s Composer of the Week, a daily show that has been going since… 1943…) or I’m sourcing far-out sounds for Radio 3’s New Music Show. That combination of proper…

quietus.title: Helen – Linda’s Head
quietus.description: Helen Linda’s Head Ahoy! Liz Harris of Grouper draws up the anchor of her 2013 slowcore side project and sets sail once more with drummer Jed Bindeman on the high seas Linda's Head by Helen On 27th March 1980 Mt. St Helens erupted. Two months later, Liz Harris (AKA Grouper) was born. In 2013, she teamed up with drummer Jed Bindeman and Scott Simmon on bass, introducing the world to their shoegaze band Helen with the double A-side single ‘Felt This Way’ / ‘Dying All The Time’. Their dreamy debut The Original Faces followed two years after with the band subsequently laying dormant… until now. The reappearance of this Pacific Northwest slowcore trio a decade later is less an eruption, more a…

quietus.title: Mercury Rev’s ‘Boces’ to be Reissued
quietus.description: The band's second studio album has been newly remastered for the updated release Photo by Steve Gullick Mercury Rev's 1993 album Boces is being reissued. The record has been newly remastered for its updated release, and will be made available on vinyl and CD. A digital release of the remaster is currently not scheduled to happen. Originally released in June 1993, Boces was Mercury Rev's second studio album, and was their final LP to feature original frontman David Baker, who was asked to leave the band shortly after they finished touring the record. It folded in elements of jazz, pop, noise, psychedelia, folk and doo-wop, among other sounds. Beggars Banquet will release Boces on 13…

quietus.title: Concrète Dschungel: Einstürzende Neubauten’s Kollaps At 45
quietus.description: Neubauten's uncompromising debut album ‘Kollaps’ is 45 years old. Jeremy Allen explores the bombed-out terrain of their West Berlin and wonders if, despite the penurious conditions, it was easier to make art then Feral musicians emerging from the rubble of bombed-out West Berlin (as composer György Ligeti described it, "a surrealist cage in which all those inside are free") and creating themselves out of their own blood and guts very much feels like a tale from another age. In a world of coffee shop startups, utilitarian computer software and ersatz bedroom electronica as aural wallpaper, building your own percussive instruments from scrap might seem primitive, complex, redundant even. But…

quietus.title: Under Wraps: John Frankenheimer’s Seconds turns 60
quietus.description: Wayne Gooderham salutes the shocking horror film that has influenced relatively many while being seen by relatively few In the early winter of 1967 Brian Wilson took a break from the fraught sessions for Smile – the Beach Boys’ planned follow-up to Pet Sounds – and treated himself to a visit to the cinema. According to Jules Siegel’s account of the evening in Goodbye Surfing, Hello God! Brian Wilson returned home even more distracted than ever: "‘I walked into that movie,’ he said in a tense, high-pitched voice, ‘and the first thing that happened was a voice from the screen said “Hello, Mr Wilson.” It completely blew my mind […] the whole thing was there. I mean my whole life. Birth and...

quietus.title: Megiapa – Intentions
quietus.description: Megiapa Intentions LA-based artist is adventurous and experimental, still emanating warmth Intentions by megiapa Born out of a period of change and movement, Intentions is a debut album that acts as a snapshot of producer, vocalist and visual artist Megiapa’s journey over the past couple of years. Featuring expressive grooves, mellow textures and an array of guest appearances from the likes of The Growth Eternal, pianist Ahmad Muhammad aka Kafari, and drummer Mekala Session, Intentions is a quietly confident collection that maps a multitude of experiences, from heartbreak to healing. Album opener ‘Open Your Eyes’ provides an alluring introduction, as a slap-bass sound welcomes you to the…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Antonio Adolfo :: S/T 1972
aquariumdrunkard.description: Antonio Adolfo hated his 1972 solo debut. Intensely. He banned it from his official discography and denounced it whenever it resurfaced online. Yet the slightly off singing may be exactly what gives the self-titled LP its charm: there’s a Robert Wyatt or Scott Walker quality to Adolfo’s naturally dramatic timbre, with little bent edges creating tension against the jazz-inflected solos, basslines and gently cinematic arrangements. The result is a strange, beautiful record its creator wanted forgotten.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Jess Williamson :: A Mile South of Heaven
aquariumdrunkard.description: Jess Williamson's Shooter Jennings-produced sixth solo album, A Mile South of Heaven , is a desert curiosity shop’s worth of inspirations: Williamson pulls storytelling techniques from Lucinda Williams’ gravel-road realism, a dash of Leonard Cohen’s everyday spirituality, and the vocal delivery of so many worn-leather country starlets.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Beach Boys :: Radiant Radish
aquariumdrunkard.description: True story: in the late ’60s, Brian Wilson opened a short-lived health-food store called Radiant Radish in West Hollywood. Untrue story: there was a Beach Boys album named after it. There wasn’t—but now, thanks to the enterprising retrogorilla YouTube channel, there is. Radiant Radish is a wonderfully strange reimagining of the Smile / Smiley Smile / Wild Honey / Friends era, rearranged into a new and surprisingly coherent whole. Eat your vega-tables.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Lagniappe Sessions :: Squirrel Flower
aquariumdrunkard.description: The nom-de-tune of Chicago-based songwriter and guitarist Ella O’Connor Williams, Squirrel Flower’s debut Lagniappe Session comes on the heels of her latest LP, Say a Prayer to the Gods of Getting Going. Here, Williams takes on four songs that found their way into her orbit by different paths over the past decade: Tunnel of Love -era Springsteen, the Alex Chilton narcotica that is Big Star’s “Kanga Roo,” Guided By Voices’ “Awful Bliss,” and Joan Osborne’s “Lumina.” Williams notes on her selections below.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Sagegazers :: A Mixtape
aquariumdrunkard.description: The Sagegazers is an ongoing project devoted to the strange and beautiful world of privately released ambient, electronic, and New Age cassette music of the 1980s and ’90s. Working from a collection of rare and often nearly undocumented recordings, the project uncovers a forgotten culture of synthesizers, home studios, spirituality, landscape, and imagination. This mix offers a journey through that world, bringing together 15 recordings that reveal the remarkable breadth, intimacy, and imagination of this largely unmapped musical culture.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Andy Boay :: Doomed
aquariumdrunkard.description: Andy Boay returns with an opus crafted with ecstatic care: a journey of reverbed vocals and guitar noodles, a lo-fi love letter, a bedroom SMiLE , and its own thing completely: Doomed . Doomed shares the same creative DNA as its brilliant predecessor, 2025’s You Took That Walk For The Two Of Us : another painstakingly crafted cassette recording, with tape manipulation galore and self-harmonies aplenty.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Jeremy Cunningham :: Passing Fires
aquariumdrunkard.description: Jeremy Cunningham makes music that seems to be perpetually slipping out of its own frame. On Passing Fires , the Chicago drummer moves from free-jazz and skronk to electronics, funk, post-rock and pop, assembling a cast of improvisers, producers and singers who keep the music in motion. There are moments of muscular rhythmic interplay, strange electronic textures, children’s voices, whispered vocals and unexpected turns. It’s an album of restless curiosity, but never restlessness for its own sake: Cunningham’s drumming provides a steady gravitational pull as the music wanders.

Werner Herzog’s first fiction film in seven years, Bucking Fastard (2026),stands as one of his most bizarre. That’s high praise for a director who’s pulled 300-plus-ton steamships over mountains ( Fitzcarraldo , 1982), hypnotized his actors ( Heart of Glass , 1976), and followed “deranged” penguins across Antarctica ( Encounters at the End of the World , 2007). In 2005, during a television interview in Italy, Giuseppe “Pino” Pelosi—AKA “The Frog”—recanted his confession about murdering Pier Paolo Pasolini on a beach in Ostia 30 years earlier. He claimed that it had been extracted by coercion and threats of violence, against both himself and his family (Pelosi was seventeen at the time). He also said that the legendary director’s death was a political killing disguised as a crime of passion—the premeditated and methodical muzzling of a “Dirty Communist.” Sergio Citti, a close friend of Pasolini, contributed to the controversy by suggesting that the filmmaker had been lured to the water…
